title: JBU vs SPU: tuition, size, location
summary: John Brown University (JBU) versus Seattle Pacific University (SPU). Also searched as SPU vs JBU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: John Brown University and Seattle Pacific University are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes reported by College Scorecard. John Brown University, located in Siloam Springs, has an undergraduate enrollment of 1,471 students, while Seattle Pacific University in Seattle enrolls 1,762 undergraduates. Tuition for in-state students at John Brown University is $31,756, which is lower compared to Seattle Pacific University's in-state tuition of $40,407. These differences highlight variations in size, location, and cost between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: John Brown University (JBU) and Seattle Pacific University (SPU) differ notably in their tuition costs. Both institutions charge the same tuition for in-state and out-of-state students, with JBU's tuition set at $31,756 and SPU's at $40,407. This indicates that JBU offers a lower tuition rate compared to SPU. Additionally, the median debt for students who complete their programs at JBU is $21,250, which is less than the $24,000 median debt reported for SPU completers. These financial figures provide insight into the relative affordability and student debt outcomes at each university.

sections.heading: Pick JBU if
paragraphs: Pick John Brown University if you prefer a private nonprofit institution with a higher admission rate and a strong completion rate.
